parts.note: to count someone in is to include them, so count can mean include

explanation.surface: A book seems to feature an aristocrat among its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link; 'include' supplies its synonym COUNT rather than acting as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a peer ranking between earl and baron, so a titled nobleman.

clue.text: Former exam relating to the countryside

parts.note: former means past, belonging to an earlier time
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An old test once set on rural matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life, shepherds and farmland, as opposed to the town.

parts.note: to whack an opponent is to thrash them soundly
Oscar is the radio alphabet code word for the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a rival called Oscar and is congratulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacko!' is a dated British exclamation of delight, roughly 'splendid!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned British cries of approval or delight, interchangeable as exclamations.

clue.text: Encourage operator to release latest of numbers

indicators.note: releasing a letter lets it go, so it drops out of the word for operator

parts.note: a surgeon performs operations, so is an operator

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one

explanation.surface: Someone urges a telephone operator to give out the newest numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to release' takes the S (last letter of 'numbers', from 'latest of') out of SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is to spur or egg someone forward, a phrasal synonym for encourage.

clue.text: Male elected to keep investment, in error

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
a stake is a share put into a venture

explanation.surface: A man voted into office holds on to his shares, wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mistaken means being wrong, which is what being in error describes.

clue.text: Back with fish to sell down the river

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: A wager on a fish that is then traded away downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone down the river is an idiom for deceiving or abandoning a trusting ally.

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
each means individually or apiece

explanation.surface: Each independent member is to be accused one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a public official is to formally charge them with misconduct.

indicators.note: the first of a word means its opening letter

parts.note: principal as an adjective means leading or chief, as in a lead role

explanation.surface: A request from the head of a polytechnic college.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request or entreaty, a verb sense of appeal.

definitions.meaning: the ... tree is a European tree related to the rowan
a car ... is its routine upkeep

explanation.surface: Looking after trees, as a gardener might.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a rowan-like tree of the genus Sorbus; the other is routine upkeep of a machine.

parts.note: in a football match the forward who scores goals is the attacker; a match also has a part that strikes

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as football, but 'match' also hints at the head of a match that is struck to light it.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre-forward in football is the attacking player whose job is scoring goals.

clue.text: Conservative inclined towards socialism is divided

definitions.note: the definition is the participle-like adjective, split in two

parts.note: the political left favours socialism

explanation.surface: A Tory leaning towards socialism is torn in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is an old past participle of cleave, meaning split apart.

parts.note: to carp is to grumble or find fault
to enter details is to write them down in a record

explanation.surface: Grumble and write off a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner is a woodworker making doors and fittings, essentially the same trade.

parts.note: under means beneath or below

indicators.note: knocked out suggests the letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Kept down in the hold, a man lay unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a man felled by a blow, but 'knocked out' is the anagram signal working on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept locked away securely is confined, as a prisoner is.

indicators.note: the word for followed stretches across the river, enclosing it

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone tracked by boat across a river while under tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan pulled behind a car is trailed, drawn along behind, which is being towed.

indicators.note: the anagrammed shoes are worn by the letter, so they go around it
muddy suggests something messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out wearing dirty slip-on shoes in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddy' rearranges LOAFERS into ALFRESO, and 'wearing' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining al fresco means eating in the open air, so outside.

clue.text: Tried to set off for US city

indicators.note: setting off, as a charge explodes, scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to depart for an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the Michigan city famed for its car industry.

indicators.note: in places the word for steady within the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means level or steady

explanation.surface: A steady earner living on a Paris street.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, especially to a business or government.

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: a country importing goods brings them inside its borders

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: Opposing a nation that brings in foreign goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means energy or vigour, as in full of go.

parts.note: even means uniform or regular
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An airline's scheduled flight route.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an air service by plane; the definition is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

parts.note: express as an adjective means explicit or definite
a newspaper prints articles

explanation.surface: A query about a story in the Daily Express.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express is a British tabloid newspaper, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'the' is called the definite article, as opposed to 'a'.

definitions.meaning: to abandon is to leave behind
a wilderness is a barren, empty region such as the Sahara

explanation.surface: Someone left stranded in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means forsake; as a noun, an arid waste land.

clue.text: Can appearing upside down humour blockhead?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being upside down means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can
wit is clever humour

explanation.surface: Could an inverted joke amuse a fool?
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or stupid person, like a dunce.

clue.text: Declare invalid must be taken round area once a year

indicators.note: the first word is taken round, enclosing the letter

parts.note: to annul a marriage is to declare it invalid

explanation.surface: A cancelled agreement must be shown around the district.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual describes something happening yearly, such as an annual festival.

definitions.meaning: a stage show by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters
the board game of kings, queens and pawns

explanation.surface: A game with songs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a 1980s stage musical and also the strategy board game it is named after.

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding or dessert
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: A pudding paired with a novel kind of vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize kernels eaten as a vegetable are sold as sweetcorn in Britain.

clue.text: Shows the way in speech in English city

indicators.note: in speech signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a guide leads, showing others the way

explanation.surface: A guide gives directions out loud in a northern city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Right about returned item — proof of purchase required

indicators.note: about means around, so the two letters go round the other piece
returned means sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a piece is an item, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A shop insists on evidence before taking back a returned item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes ECEIP, which 'about' sets between the two letters for right; 'required' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the slip a shop gives as evidence that goods were bought.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A workman who is partly responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanic in its old sense means a manual worker or craftsman, as Shakespeare's rude mechanicals.
